headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared git/workspace plus Claude Code’s MCP and broad egress; compliance risk is elevated by closed-source, third-party API handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider and Claude Code both operate on repo files and shared git state, so attacker-controlled content in one agent’s edits can be read and acted on by the other. The pathway is plausible in default terminal workflows, though not as direct as a shared MCP channel. No clipboard or browser bridge is shown, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or working tree, injected instructions in files can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Use separate repos or branches per agent.
Add a human review step before either agent consumes the other’s output.
Prefix untrusted file content as data, not instructions.
Disable shared workspace access during autonomous runs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write repo files and git history, so sensitive source code or secrets in the workspace can flow between them. Claude Code also sends requests to api.anthropic.com, while Aider uses user-configured model providers, creating a default path for workspace contents to leave the host. This is a medium-risk shared-workspace leakage pattern.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared repository, both agents can access them.
IF Claude Code transmits context to api.anthropic.com, workspace contents may leave the host.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo before running either agent.
Use a scrubbed test checkout for agent collaboration.
Restrict Claude Code to non-sensitive directories.
Rotate any credentials that were present in the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write access, shell execution, and modify git state in the same shared repo/workspace. Aider explicitly shares state via git repo, and Claude Code shares via filesystem and git only, so concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default and can cause irreversible repo history damage.
conditions: IF both agents operate concurrently on the same git repository, conflicting writes can occur.
IF either agent rewrites history or auto-commits while the other is editing, repository state can be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize edits with a simple lock file.
Require manual git review before commit.
Pause one agent while the other is applying patches.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider’s auto-commit workflow and Claude Code’s agentic terminal behavior make it likely that one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without strong verification. If Claude Code acts on Aider-generated patches or summaries as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or shell actions. The pair lacks a documented cross-checking barrier, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Claude Code consumes Aider-generated diffs or summaries without verification, mistakes can propagate.
IF either agent executes shell or git actions based on the other’s output, downstream errors can become persistent.
mitigations: Require a second-pass review before any commit.
Ask each agent to cite file paths and line numbers.
Compare outputs against the original task before acting.
Limit one agent to drafting and the other to verification.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code is closed-source and sends data to Anthropic’s API, while Aider is open-source and can use user-configured providers. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create a policy mismatch because one agent’s outbound path is vendor-controlled and not documented as residency-safe here. The other agent is not cited because the compliance concern is driven mainly by Claude Code’s external API path.
conditions: IF regulated data such as EU PII or secrets is stored in the shared workspace, Claude Code may transmit it to a third-party API.
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the configured providers, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Use a provider configuration approved for the data class.
Review retention settings before running either agent.
Run the pair only on synthetic or redacted data.
